tasks.title: Patch DeepGEMM for SM121 paged-sparse MQA-logits kernels in a fork image
tasks.notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-11-03 (QUESTIONS.md #53, answering CLR-BRIEF Q1 option c): build it ourselves rather than track upstream. This was the external gate blocking two survey arms; it is now the work itself. Scope: DeepGEMM asserts `arch_major == 10` (SM100) in `csrc/apis/attention.hpp:301` for the paged-sparse MQA-logits kernels, and GB10 is SM121. Start from the retained v1-fallback build `dsv41-c3-reconciled:103ad321@sha256:13f686b3...` - the 2026-10-26 c3 re-port verdict already failed on this same assert, so its tree is the natural base. Deliverables: (1) read the assert's neighbourhood and decide whether it guards a real hard-coded assumption (tile shapes, TMA descriptors); if it does, this is writing kernels for a new architecture, not patching a line, and that verdict is itself the finding to report before more GPU time goes in; (2) if the guard is conservative, patch it, keep the negative controls, and prove kernel numerics against the SM100 reference on a shape that fits one node; (3) publish the fork image and record its digest so `w4-survey-arm3-indexer-scoring` and `w4-survey-arm5-trtllm-mla` can start. Gate policy: the image is the artifact - a boot is not proof, a numeric comparison is. Day-scale with unknown risk; if step (1) says the assumption is real, come back with that finding and a cost estimate rather than burning the day.

STEP (1) VERDICT 2026-11-03 (read-only, no GPU time): **real architectural dependency — but already ported off-branch, so this is a source pin/backport, not kernel authoring.** Detail: `mad-science/DEEPSEEK.md` §20. The assert is a family gate with no fallback (both sparse logits entry points call `launch_sm100_sparse_mqa_logits` unconditionally), and the SM100 kernel needs TMEM alloc/`tcgen05.mma` block-scaled MXF4/MXF8F6F4/`tcgen05.ld`/`tcgen05.cp`/`tcgen05.commit` — none of which exist on SM121 (tcgen05 targets are SM_100/103/107/110 only). INDEPENDENT KILLER, more final than the instructions: the kernel's smem plan is 232,448 B (`heuristics/sm100.hpp:16`, asserted at `sm100_sparse_mqa_logits.hpp:80,166`) and a GB10 CTA caps at 99 KiB — 2.29x over, so it cannot launch even if the opcodes were conjured. WHAT CHANGES THE COST: `deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM` `nv_dev` b64107f (2026-09-24) ships `sm120_fp8_fp4_sparse_mqa_logits` (570 lines) plus its launcher, with the four arch gates widened to `== 10 or == 12`, `mma.sync...kind::mxf8f6f4.block_scale` accepted by ptxas for sm_121a, and the kernel guard `__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 1200 and < 1300` covering GB10's 1210 — same pybind API, same metadata layout, and it queries device smem instead of hard-coding it. THE HOLE: `sgl-project/DeepGEMM` dev (the tree an SGLang image pins) has SM120 for DENSE and paged MQA logits but no sparse SM120 kernel and still asserts arch==10 at `attention.hpp:382`. REVISED COST: pin nv_dev 6-10 h to first sparse numerics (1-2 days to a green arm-3 boot), backport onto the sgl fork 10-16 h, kernel authoring 40-80 h — the row's literal reading was the 40-80 h case and is no longer the plan. PRECONDITIONS the port must satisfy: page stride `% 512 == 0` (page_kv 128 passes, 64 fails — att5's index page size is 64), a narrowed head contract (SM120 kernel is fixed at 32 heads / head_dim 128 / BLOCK_Q 2), and zero upstream test coverage for the SM120 sparse path, so numerics must be gated before any serve boot. FALSIFIER: one kernel-level paged sparse run in the retained `dsv41-c3-reconciled:103ad321` image, reading the emitted arch from the JIT line and diffing numerics against the torch reference — no serve, no quartet.

ROUTE CHOSEN 2026-11-03 (owner): **backport onto `sgl-project/DeepGEMM` dev**, 10-16 h to first sparse numerics. Why not the faster nv_dev pin (6-10 h): nv_dev is six weeks behind the tree SGLang actually integrates, so the pin buys speed with API drift, while the backport lands on the tree already in use and confines adaptation risk to the contiguous tail-flag path rather than the paged path arm 3 needs. Estimate set to 13 h (midpoint). PRECONDITION that may park it anyway: the SM120 launcher requires a 512-byte page stride and att5's index page size is 64 (64 x 132 = 8448, mod 512 = 256), so the backport has to extend the stride contract or serve page_kv 128 — resolve that arithmetic before writing code, because it decides whether the console arm can use the kernel at all.

STRIDE DECISION 2026-11-03 (owner): **widen the stride contract inside the backport** — keep att5's `dsv41_index_page_size: 64` and teach the SM120 launcher the SM100 128-byte rule (or handle both), rather than changing the serving arm's page layout. Recorded risk: that is a kernel-contract change with zero upstream test coverage, so numerics must be gated against the torch reference before any serve boot.

PRECONDITION RESOLVED 2026-11-03 (source read at both trees, no hardware). The 512-byte page stride is NOT a kernel contract and NOT in the backport target: it exists only in deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM@nv_dev `sm120_fp8_fp4_sparse_mqa_logits.hpp:81`, while sgl-project/DeepGEMM@dev has no SM120 sparse kernel at all (sparse gates still `arch_major == 10` at csrc/apis/attention.hpp:358,389,425,459,494) and takes the page pitch from the tensor with only a 16-byte global-stride check (runtime_utils.hpp:179-181) plus a `% 128` page rule (attention.hpp:474-478). The kernel addresses pages by page_idx*page_stride and moves KV as 16-byte cp.async, so 512 is a guard, not a need: nv_dev's own test satisfies it at page_kv=64 by padding the pitch (test_attention.py:674-681). The consumer's page is not 64 B either — 64 slots x 68/132 B = 4,352/8,448 B — and with the sparse flag ON sglang returns page size 128 (deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:534-542) giving 8,704/16,896 B, exact multiples of 512. Fix = one line, `% 512` -> `% 128`. THE REAL GATE is SGLang's `configurer.py:54` `DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL = is_sm100`, which excludes SM121 (utils/common.py:284-293), so the backported kernel is unreachable on GB10 until that is opened: the work is kernel-present + gate-open, two parts, and the 10-16 h estimate stands for the backport itself. DISPATCH CLAIM 2026-11-07: a worker (`deepgemm-sm121`) is on the SM121 patch and build for the paged-sparse MQA-logits family - base `dsv41-c3-reconciled:103ad321@sha256:13f686b3...`, the `arch_major == 10` assert at `csrc/apis/attention.hpp:301`; this is a research/build task with no inference boot yet. Dispatch state, not a measurement: it clears when the build verdict lands.

DONE 2026-11-07 - built and gated on the head against base `dsv41-c3-reconciled:103ad321@sha256:13f686b3...`. Image `dsv41-sm121-dg:0.2.0` = `sha256:1778ec428bc448b4111b2170de3631d7a337da2065d83d3264d198f0fe46c76b`, local tag only, nothing pushed (the c3 arm's transport is `--transfer-mode local`); build rc=0 in about 70 s, image 33.9 GB on disk. The patch is **guard-widening plus the SM120 kernel ported from `nv_dev` b64107f2, not kernel authoring**: `attention.hpp` arch gates widened to `== 10 or == 12` with the dispatch, page stride 512 -> 128, `sm100`/`sm120` impls plus a new launcher, and the test arch filter. Kernel-level gate **8/8 PASS** - MXFP8 and MXFP4 x page_kv 128/64 x sparse_block_kv 8/16, `calc_diff` 1.3e-05 against an FP32 torch reference, 4 replays bitwise equal, negative control catches a corrupted page; `nvcc --cubin` exit 0 for both `sm_121a` and `sm_121f`, and the image prints `DEEPGEMM_PAGED_SPARSE_MQA_LOGITS` True. This CLEARS the DeepGEMM half of both blocked survey arms (their notes updated in this pass; they stay blocked on the quartet window, not on the kernel).

Pre-existing defect recorded so it is not misread as this port: SM120 *dense contiguous* MXFP8 logits go NaN on GB10 **in the untouched base image too** (2,097,096 of 2,097,152 entries non-finite, `dbg_contig_dense.py`), and because the SM120 dense *paged* reference asserts `arch_major == 10`, the numerics gate used the torch FP32 reference rather than a dense-path cross-check. tasks.title: Feasibility: mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B-NVFP4 (1T total / 52B active MoE) on the WOPR fleet
tasks.notes:
Study, not a boot. Measured from the Hub API 2026-10-29: 610.03 GB of weights (index total_size 610030457408; 32 x ~20 GB consolidated shards, 44 files), ungated/public, Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License (modified MIT, commercial use allowed, MaaS resale needs a separate license). Shape from params.json: 72 layers, dim 6144, MoE hidden_dim 24576, 64 heads / 64 kv heads with MLA (kv_lora_rank 512, qk_rope 64, qk_nope 64, v_head_dim 128), DeepSeek-style DSA sparse attention (topk 2048, 32 heads), kv_sharing across layers, 1M context (yarn factor 2048), an embedded DSpark speculative draft head, and multimodal text+image input. ARITHMETIC THAT DECIDES IT: a node is 128 GB unified, so TP=4 puts 152.5 GB of weights on each rank before any KV, activation or CUDA-graph reservation - infeasible with no room to argue; TP=6 across ALL SIX nodes is the only shape that could carry the weights (101.7 GB/rank, ~26 GB/rank left for KV, activations and CUDA graphs) - and 64 heads do not divide by 6, so even that needs an engine-side answer first; TP=8 exceeds the fleet. Note the displacement cost of any TP=6 attempt: it takes every node including the four running the production serve, so it is a declared full-fleet window with production stopped, not a background job. node_cost is blank on purpose: this row is a STUDY with no node time. Deliverable: a short verdict with the three candidate paths and their costs - (a) further quantization to ~2.5-3 bpw to reach ~4 ranks (checkpoint conversion project, needs a bits-per-weight target derived from the 128 GB budget minus KV), (b) a rented 8-rank box where the published NVFP4 checkpoint fits as-is, (c) park it. Also record what the DSpark draft head and DSA would need from SGLang/vLLM versions, since a mismatch is a second, independent blocker.

DONE 2026-11-03 — VERDICT: park it. TP=4 dies on weight bytes (152.51 GB = 142.03 GiB per rank, 20.3 GiB over the 121.69 GiB device), TP=6 on head divisibility and then bytes, the 6-rank hybrids on bytes, TP=8 exceeds the fleet. The only path that serves the checkpoint as published is a rented 8-rank box (76.25 GB/rank, 8 heads/rank; indexed $3.50-8.19 GPU-hr on 2026-10-27 = $28-66/hr node). CORRECTION to this row's own arithmetic: the '~26 GB/rank left' figure used the 128 GB marketing number and ignored the OS reserve — against the 103.7 GiB usable line TP=6 leaves **9.0 GiB**, and **3.0 GiB** once vision (3.41 GB) and the DSpark head (4.20 GB) are replicated per rank. Also corrected: 63 KV-bearing layers, not 72 (nine layers share layer 35), and 1M-context KV is 43.96 GB **per sequence**. Recomputed weights: 610,030,457,408 B, 32 header sums equal index.total_size exactly, 1.0532 T params, 4.634 bpw overall, 94.9% of bytes in routed experts. A requantisation path would need 3.11 bpw overall at 8k and 2.78 at 1M (routed experts 2.94 / 2.60) sourced from the 1,060.6 GB FP8 base, never from the NVFP4 packing. SECOND, INDEPENDENT BLOCKER: no engine supports the architecture — vLLM main has no `mistral_large4` (highest is `mistral_large_3`) and neither SGLang main nor the pinned `mistral-large-4` tree (c10e0e17, 444 commits behind) has `mistral_large4`/`le_chonk`; the two vendor images are forks built 2026-10-29, one with `VLLM_BUILD_COMMIT=unknown`. Displacement: TP=6 takes all six nodes, four of which serve production and are the baseline of every TP=4 head-to-head cell.

tasks.title: Survey Ornith-1.5-122B quantisations and finetunes for drafter compatibility (incl. uncensored/abliterated/cyber)
tasks.notes:
OWNER REQUEST 2026-10-30 (normal priority). Question: which 122B quantisations and finetunes pair well with incoai/Ornith-1.5-122B-DFlash2, and is there an uncensored/abliterated/cybersecurity finetune or quant that does? Method: (1) enumerate Hub candidates for the 122B base and its finetunes (nvfp4/fp8/awq/gguf, plus abliterated/uncensored/cyber derivatives) and record architecture + hidden_size + layer count, because the drafter hard-codes hidden_size 3072 and target_layer_ids [1,7,14,20,26,32,39,45] — a finetune with a different depth or width cannot use it at all; (2) acceptance is a property of the target's hidden states, so a finetune must keep the same layer geometry; (3) GGUF targets need mask_embedding.safetensors wired in or draft acceptance roughly halves (card, 'GGUF targets'); (4) rank candidates and hand the top three to a boot arm. Deliverable: a table in recipes/ornith/README.md plus one drafted recipe per viable candidate.

DONE 2026-11-03. Census: 67 derivative repos for the 122B (Hub base_model tags + name sweep), 9 finetune-tagged, 47 quantized-tagged, plus a 1,008-repo sweep of the whole Ornith family. GEOMETRY GATE proven in engine source rather than exercised: the drafter is hidden_size 3072 / num_target_layers 48 / target_layer_ids [1,7,14,20,26,32,39,45] / vocab 248320 / block_size 16; a different depth raises ValueError in SGLang v0.5.22 `resolve_target_layer_ids` (dflash_utils.py) and a different width breaks the selector shape (dflash.py), and no candidate in the family changes either, so 0 geometry rejects. **THE FINDING THAT PARKS A SUB-LANE**: the published `mask_embedding.safetensors` is read by NEITHER engine we run - SGLang 0.5.22 merges only `mask_embedding.pt` (literal filename in dflash_worker_v2.py, plus mask_token_id/per_position fields the safetensors lacks) and llama.cpp at the lane pin a37cc4610 takes the target's own tok_embd row with no mask-file input at all - and dealignai's own GB10 measurement of that pairing is parity (26.23 vs 26.27 t/s), so no GGUF DFlash2 arm was drafted. SECURITY ANSWER: there is no cybersecurity 122B finetune - devsecllm is a rank-3 Heretic ablation of the vendor NVFP4 export published for blue-team work (CyberBench 62.5 vs 61.3, HumanEval 93.3 both, NIAH 20/20) and dealignai is the general refusal-removed build (MMLU -1.69 pp, HarmBench 309/320); cyber / OBLITERATED / heretic naming exists only on 9B/35B/397B. Every 122B candidate is MIT (dongnhdev Apache-2.0; the scottlowry/krisfremen oQ repos declare no licence at all), so the two eval-only banners are house policy on refusal-removed weights, not licence-driven. RANKED: dealignai (smallest fitting target, uncensored, bundles the drafter), devsecllm (byte-identical layout to the vendor, highest acceptance prior), cyankiwi int4 (the only non-NVFP4 family). New arms use d4, not the card's 15. UNMEASURED: acceptance for all three - they are drafted arms, and the two security builds rest on geometry plus their own cards; the cyankiwi repo is labelled AWQ-INT4 but its config says quant_method compressed-tensors (int4 g32, 1430 ignore entries), so an SGLang refusal on that mixed layout is the declared falsifier.

BOOT RESULT 2026-11-03, arm 1 of 3 (`zz-dealignai-...-uncensored-dflash2-sglang`, `.30`): **the serve is up and generating, but the output is incoherent** — llama-benchy's coherence probe failed (`Expected 'Paris'. Got: ...`) after its own warmups had passed. Direct probes on the live endpoint, temperature 0: WITHOUT the thinking kwarg `content=''` and `reasoning_content` is token salad ('ess-de chose midstinal二是.pass.append ...'); WITH `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false` `content` is salad and `reasoning_content` is null. So this is NOT the empty-content reasoning-channel class — the model itself emits garbage under this engine/quant pairing, which is exactly the `[INFERENCE]` the survey flagged: 'acceptance for all three arms is unmeasured; the two security builds rest on geometry plus their own cards'. Geometry being compatible does not make the checkpoint usable. FALSIFIER to run before blaming the drafter: the same recipe with the speculative flags absent (the `zz-ornith-1.5-122b-nvfp4-nospec-sglang` pattern) — coherent there means the DFlash2 drafter is wrong for this finetune despite matching geometry; still salad means the quant/template/engine pairing is the problem. Do not record a decode rate for this arm until one of those is answered.

ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION 2026-11-03 19:30 ET (read from the live container's serve log, `docker exec … /tmp/sparkrun_serve.log`): the arm is running with **`accept len: 1.00, accept rate: 0.00`** — the incoai drafter is accepting NOTHING against this finetune. That changes what the salad can be blamed on: the earlier note in this row said 'the model itself emits garbage', and that attribution is withdrawn, because both probes ran with speculative decoding ON. A drafter that accepts nothing should degrade to the target's own tokens, so either the DFLASH verification path is corrupting the decode for a target/drafter pair whose hidden states disagree, or the weights are bad — and only a nospec run separates those. PREDICTION for arm 2 (`zz-devsecllm-…-dflash2-sglang`): it uses the same incoai drafter, so it should show the same accept rate and the same salad; if it does, stop the family's boots and run the nospec falsifier instead of spending a third hour. Owner's chosen order (finish arms 2 and 3) is being followed, but arm 2's acceptance number decides whether arm 3 runs.

ARM 1 CLOSED 2026-11-03 19:40 ET, rc=5: the house suite had run 65 minutes against a serve emitting salad at ~10 t/s, so it was stopped deliberately — rc=5 there means 'the bench produced no artifact', not 'the launch failed', and the two must not be confused when reading boot.log. Arm 2 (devsecllm, same incoai drafter, same abliterated-target shape) started 19:41.

ROOT CAUSE ESTABLISHED 2026-11-03 19:50 ET (primary sources, both sides). `dealignai/Ornith-1.5-122B-UNCENSORED-NVFP4` declares per-layer `FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN` on 308 layers INCLUDING `lm_head`; SGLang v0.5.22 `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig.get_quant_method` implements only FP8 / block-FP8 / MXFP8 / NVFP4 / W4A16_NVFP4 and falls through to `UnquantizedLinearMethod()` (`modelopt_quant.py:1040`), with `None` for fused MoE (`:1069`); the string occurs 0 times in modelopt_quant.py, fp8.py, compressed_tensors.py and quantization/__init__.py. So 308 layers load unquantized from fp8-serialized weights and lose their per-channel scale — boots, ready, garbage. The live serve log's `accept rate: 0.00` is the SAME defect at the drafter (DFLASH borrows the target lm_head), so it does not indict the drafter. The natural falsifier is already boots: devsecllm's export is quant-clean (W4A16_NVFP4 193 + FP8 156, lm_head W4A16_NVFP4) with the same drafter/template/parsers, so coherent-devsecllm-plus-salad-dealignai confirms it outright; the two authored probe arms are HELD and only earn boots if devsecllm is also salad. cyankiwi is compressed-tensors pack-quantized (a different loader) and answers a separate question. Disposition to record once devsecllm reports: dealignai becomes a recorded negative with the re-export / engine-bump follow-ups named in the lane doc.

DISPOSITION SPLIT so the two remaining legs are not one bet: dealignai is a recorded NEGATIVE (export layout, engine can't load it — follow-ups are an engine bump or a re-export using implemented algo names). devsecllm is the control and, if coherent, the family's first servable 122B finetune. cyankiwi tests compressed-tensors loading, a third distinct question.

CONFIRMED BY NATURAL EXPERIMENT 2026-11-03 20:15 ET, one boot each, identical flags, same drafter: dealignai (FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN x308) -> token salad, accept rate 0.00; devsecllm (W4A16_NVFP4 x193 + FP8 x156, head W4A16) -> 'The capital of France is Paris.', accept rate 0.62-0.64. Only the export layout differs, so hypothesis 1 is confirmed and the drafter/template/parser hypotheses are retired. The two probe arms are retired UNSPENT and stay in-tree as the falsifiers for a future misbehaving export. devsecllm is the family's first servable 122B finetune; its own disposition (promote past zz- or keep eval-only) waits on its ladder/suite numbers, which run-arm.sh is producing. cyankiwi (compressed-tensors) still untested — separate loader, separate question.

tasks.title: Does Python 3.14 beat 3.12 for vLLM/SGLang? Measure the interpreter's share of serving
tasks.notes:
OWNER REQUEST 2026-10-30 (high priority). Question: does Python 3.14 reduce the Python-side overhead that caps a GPU-bound executor, and does it show up in a serving cell? Wheel survey done first (PyPI, 2026-10-30): torch 2.15.0 has **8 cp314 wheels**, triton 3.9.0 ships cp314 and cp314t (free-threaded), tokenizers 0.23.3 has 7 cp314, uvloop 0.23.0 has 12 — so the runtime layer is available. **The engines are not:** sglang 0.5.23 publishes 0 cp314 (2 cp312), vllm 0.32.0 publishes no cp31x wheels at all on PyPI, and flashinfer-python / sgl-kernel publish none for either — so Leg B needs a source build of the engine plus flashinfer against cp314. Leg A (cheap, no GPU image): microbenchmark the Python-side per-token work under 3.12 vs 3.14 vs 3.14t on the same host — tokenizer/detokenizer round-trip, SSE chunk JSON encode, an asyncio request loop at 1k-10k QPS, and the specializing-interpreter/JIT effect on plain loops. Report each as ns/op with the 3.12 baseline, because that is the ceiling any serving gain can have. Leg B (expensive): source-build sglang (or vllm) under cp312 and cp314 in one CUDA base, same model and profile, then the campaign ladder extended to **c1/c2/c5/c10/c50/c100** — Python overhead grows with concurrency, so c10 alone cannot see it — plus a short-output shape where per-token Python cost dominates. **One node, alternating boots** (A/B interleaved) so node variance cannot be mistaken for an interpreter effect; two nodes would confound it. Falsifier: no serving cell outside +/-3 % of the 3.12 baseline while the Leg A microbench shows gains => conclude the limiter is GPU/scheduler, not the interpreter, and record that as the answer. Also test 3.14t: a no-GIL build trades single-thread speed for concurrency, which is exactly the detokenizer/scheduler contention shape. LEG A RESULT (measured 2026-10-30 on the workstation, uv-managed interpreters on BOTH sides so build flags cannot explain a delta; `tools/py-runtime-bench.py`, best of 3, ns/op). Cases a newer interpreter can move are separated from cases it cannot: C/Rust-backed paths are the control. | case | kind | 3.12 | 3.14 | 3.14t | | pure loop | Python | 80.1 | **48.6 (-39 %)** | 52.0 (-35 %) | | pure-Python detokenizer | Python | 1995 | **1515 (-24 %)** | 1635 (-18 %) | | asyncio scheduler | Python | 295 957 | **214 725 (-27 %)** | 285 438 (-3.6 %) | | request-body json.loads | C | 3426 | 3111 (-9.2 %) | 3161 (-7.7 %) | | streaming-delta json.dumps | C | 3502 | 3472 (-0.9 %) | **3768 (+7.6 %)** | | bytes->str detokenize | C/Rust | 113.4 | 110.1 (-2.9 %) | 109.7 (-3.2 %) | Reading, and it is the opposite of the first draft's: 3.14's gain is real but it lives in the **Python-level** paths (-24 to -39 %), while the C/Rust paths it cannot touch are flat or worse -- and free-threaded 3.14t is **worse on every C path** (+7.6 % json.dumps) and no better than 3.14 on asyncio. So the expected engine win depends on how much of that engine's per-token path is Python: an executor with a Rust tokenizer and C JSON has almost none, while a Python detokenizer or Python scheduler loop has a measurable share. That is why Leg B must record WHICH tokenizer/JSON path the built engine uses. Caveat: asyncio is the noisiest case (3.12 read 251k-296k across runs), so quote it as a range, not a point. WHEELS VERIFIED for Linux/arm64 (the fleet's platform, PyPI 2026-10-30): torch 2.15.0 publishes 4 manylinux cp314 wheels including `cp314-cp314-manylinux_2_28_aarch64` AND `cp314-cp314t-...-aarch64`; triton 3.9.0 publishes 2 manylinux cp314 wheels but **only cp314t (free-threaded)** on both arches. So on arm64 a GIL 3.14 build would need triton from another source, while a 3.14t build has a complete wheel set -- which is the opposite of what the benchmark says is desirable. Prereqs for Leg B: sglang 0.5.23 has no cp314 wheel and flashinfer/sgl-kernel none at all, so the engine is a source build either way. Method note kept: a first pass compared the distro 3.14 build against uv's 3.12 and read 3.14 slower on every case -- build configuration, not the interpreter.

LEG A DONE 2026-11-03 (workstation, `tools/py-runtime-bench.py --repeat 5` under CPython 3.12.14 / 3.14.6 / 3.14.9-free-threaded): the specializing interpreter delivers its documented win exactly where it was promised and nowhere else - `loop` 79 -> 48 ns (0.612x) - while the cases that dominate a real token get SLOWER: `json` 1.027x, `detok` 1.058x, `pydetok` 0.909x, `httparse` 0.910x, `asyncio` 0.870x; 3.14t is slower still on `json` (1.063x). Net per-token Python cost moves 5.10 us -> 5.03 us, i.e. 1.4%. CEILING: 5.1 us against a 73-94 ms step on the abliterated arm is 0.005-0.007% of the step, so the available 1.4% improvement is 0.013% of a decode cell - below the ladder's own run-to-run spread. VERDICT: Leg B (source-build sglang/vllm plus flashinfer against cp314, days of work) is RETIRED on this arithmetic, not deferred; keep 3.12/3.13 with the wheels the engines publish. Reopen only on a cell where Python-side time is a visible fraction of wall time - e.g. a CPU-only serve (`kev`/`laya`) under c50+, where the interpreter competes with matmul instead of a GPU. Free-threaded is not a fleet option: no cp314t engine wheels exist and 3.14t is slower on every per-token case but `pydetok`.

tasks.title: Sweep DFlash2 draft tokens 4/8/15 on the 122B NVFP4 arm — does a smaller block recover batching?
tasks.notes:
Follow-up to the 2026-10-30 A/B, where the drafter was +21.6 % at c1 but -24/-41/-47 % at c2/c5/c10 and prefill collapsed 1800 -> 661 by c2, while the no-spec baseline RISES (28.95 -> 48.97). Hypothesis: a 15-token draft block cannot be amortised across a batch, so verification contention eats the gain — MTP's 3 tokens DID scale on vLLM (39.3 -> 81.9). Method: three boots of zz-ornith-1.5-122b-nvfp4-dflash2-sglang with -o speculative_draft_tokens=4 / 8 / 15, same window and node, ladder to c10 each; compare each against the baseline's cells in the same window, never across nights. Outcome that would matter: a setting that keeps most of the +22 % c1 win while staying within ~10 % of the baseline at c5. If no setting does, record that DFLASH cannot batch on this engine and stop spending boots on it.

LAUNCHED 2026-11-03 12:01 ET, on the head and nowhere else. Preflight: `.30`/`.35` both at 0 containers, no `.local/fleet-window.lock` (single-node job needs no window); image `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.22@sha256:e3a4f060...` present on `.30`; both snapshots complete (Ornith-1.5-122B-NVFP4 21 entries, incoai/Ornith-1.5-122B-DFlash2 5 entries, 0 `.incomplete`); render verified `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4` in the served command, so `-o speculative_draft_tokens=N` really reaches the engine (the default is 15 with a placeholder). Run the driver there, from `~/src/sparkrun-recipe-registry`. Three legs, one node, one window, 30 s between them; each leg boots, ladders, stops its task by id and re-counts containers and volumes. RESULT 2026-11-03 (three legs on `.30`, one window; driver log ends `=== sweep complete 2026-11-03T13:08:40-05:00`, legs rc=0 at 12:22 / 12:43 / 13:08): ladder `tg128` aggregate c1 / c5 / c10 = d4 38.36 / 54.35 / 51.12, d8 44.59 / 40.64 / 40.06, d15 31.04 / 27.95 / 26.83 t/s, house 29/30 on every leg (TC-14 partial), so only the 4-token block keeps rising with concurrency. Receipts `~/benchmarks/tp12-20261103/zz-ornith-1.5-122b-nvfp4-dflash2-sglang-d{4,8,15}/` (`ladder.csv`, `house.{csv,json,log,yaml}`). The verdict against the pre-registered outcome is the holder's, so state stays `running`.

DONE 2026-11-03, four legs in one window on `.30` (d4 21 min, d8 20 min, d15 24 min, control 22 min), same digest/weights/knobs, only the draft count varying. VERDICT: **d4 meets the criterion** - +31.1% at C1, +51.5% C2, +16.3% C5, +4.1% C10 against the same-window control (29.27/37.03/46.75/49.10), and +73% per-request latency at C10 (18.27 vs 10.55), so the aggregate parity is real work moved. d8 REJECTED: best single-stream (44.59, +52.3%) then -18.4% by C10. d15 (card default) is WORSE THAN NO DRAFTER past C2: -18.7/-40.2/-45.4%. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS EFFECTIVE STREAMS (`agg / per-request`), not the aggregate: control 4.66x at C10, d4 2.80x, d8 1.57x, **d15 0.76x** - below 1.0 means its requests never overlapped, so its C2/C5/C10 rows are SERIAL measurements wearing concurrency labels and must never be tabled beside d4's as the same experiment. CROSS-CHECK: yesterday's cross-night control 28.95/48.97 reproduces today at 29.27/49.10 (1.1% / 0.3%), so the old bar was sound and the drafter legs were what needed a same-window control. TRAP RECORDED: `--speculative-algorithm NONE` is NOT a way to disable spec-decode - the parser accepts it (from_string returns NONE) but beside the draft-path and draft-token flags it leaves a serve child dead behind a live container (readiness never reached, 0 serve logs, rc=4), which is why the control is a separate recipe. tasks.title: Retire the TODO.md protocol: queue.json becomes the register, with the tooling and skills to carry it
tasks.notes: Owner instruction 2026-10-30, driver = **token efficiency**. Measured today: mad-science/TODO.md is **3304 lines / 371 KB (~93k tokens)** and every board tick, closeout and planning round reads it whole; queue.json is **801 lines / 86 KB for 54 tasks** and renders as a short ordered list. That is the win — a register a session can afford to read every cycle, and one machine-checkable source instead of prose plus a mirror. SCOPE, in three parts. (A) SCHEMA + TOOLING: extend queue.json and tools/task-queue.py so the queue carries what TODO.md carries today — `decisions` (the `# DECISIONS` block: settled calls with date and rationale), `questions` (QUESTIONS.md rows: global never-reused numbering, `status: open|answered <date>`, provenance, asked) and per-task `evidence` (receipt path), plus `render --board` producing the STATUS Work-queue rows and `render --md` a human page; an importer that walks TODO.md once and emits tasks with ids, estimates, states and lane sections preserved, so the migration is mechanical rather than retyped. KEEP the invariants the protocol carries: a task closes only with a receipt, an answered question keeps its number, nothing is deleted without a surviving home. (B) SKILLS TO WRITE: one `sparkrun-queue-protocol` skill (add/claim/close, states, where evidence lives, how the board and closeout read it) replacing the TODO.md instructions; update `status-board-refresh` (its Work-queue row names TODO.md as the source of record), `sparkrun-registry-session-closeout` (§1 is a TODO checkbox flip) and AGENTS.md's register paragraph in the same pass — the routing rule is stated in four places today and they must not disagree. (C) SKILLS TO THE ATTIC: the ones whose procedure IS the retired protocol — mad-science-todo-archive, mad-science-todo-planning-round, archive-completed-items-between-docs, planning-register-session-readiness, sync-workdoc-with-verified-state, consolidate-mad-science-notes (step 3 shrinks 'the corresponding TODO.md items') — plus the repo skills that write `- [ ]` items: sparkrun-recipe-revision-drift-survey, sparkrun-revision-pin-survey, sparkrun-lane-verification (step 5 says numbers go in TODO.md). Archive location `attic/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` as tracked files, each with a one-line header naming what replaced it, plus a redirect line in the new protocol skill; the global managed copies are then deleted from ~/.omp/agent/managed-skills (never edit a user-authored skill). COMPLETION TEST: (1) TODO.md reduced to a pointer stub naming queue.json and the protocol skill, with every open item present as a task id — the 49 open `- [ ]` items and all 54+ queue entries accounted one-for-one; (2) `task-queue.py check` green and `render --board` byte-identical to the board's Work-queue table; (3) every skill above archived or rewritten, verified by a grep for TODO.md across `.omp/skills` and `~/.omp/agent/managed-skills` returning only intentional provenance mentions; (4) a measured before/after of the bytes the status-board tick must read, recorded in the commit that lands it. ORDERING: (A) first and proven with the board (the highest-frequency reader), then (B) and (C) together — writing the skill before the tooling exists teaches a protocol that does not work. **PLAN WRITTEN 2026-10-30** (`.scratch/migrate-todo/PLAN.md`, 28.8 KB): schema delta (schema_version, questions_next, questions[], decisions[], per-task lane/evidence/detail/board) with a worked object per field; 11 command changes incl. `render --board` reproducing the board's 20-row table, `queue --brief`, `check --strict`, and a one-pass `import-todo`; an 11-row skill disposition table plus the new `sparkrun-queue-protocol` outline; a 15-row protocol-text table covering the five same-commit places (`mad-science/QUEUE.md:20-21` + its §Relationship, `mad-science/README.md:53-55`, `AGENTS.md:110`/`:415-421`, `mad-science/AGENTS.md:28-31`) and the trailing citations (25 tracked files carry a TODO.md literal today); migration order with per-step reversibility. **Measured token budget: 521.6 KB (~130k tokens) read per status tick today vs 188-214 KB (~47-54k) after, -59 to -64%; register-only read 450.2 KB -> ~140 KB.** Biggest failure mode is syncthing last-writer-wins on queue.json, made silent because JSON stays valid while task rows vanish - the counter is an id census against HEAD. **One defect found and FIXED already** (independent of the migration): `tools/task-queue.py:_save()` wrote the shared register non-atomically, so a sync mid-write could publish a torn file; it now writes tmp + `os.replace`, preserves the register's mode, cleans up on failure, and has two guards including a failure-injection test that asserts the register is byte-identical after a failed replace.

tasks.notes:
`lfm3_vl`, 1918.2M, class `AutoModelForImageTextToText`, GGUF mirror `LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B-GGUF`. Same hybrid conv/attention language stack as `liquidai-lfm3-1.7b-arm` plus a vision encoder, so `trust_remote_code` remains mandatory and the footprint needs measuring (tower is resident, image tokens share the context). Instrument: standard suite for the tool-calling/VL cells - do not reuse the text arm's memory model or its ladder numbers. Verify engine support before boot: llama.cpp through the mirror's GGUF + its mmproj companion (find the exact `mmproj-*.gguf` name in the mirror rather than guessing), vLLM/SGLang `lfm3_vl` UNVERIFIED. INSTRUMENT CORRECTION 2026-11-07 (row stays queued; no state flip): the “standard suite through the recipe path” cell promised above does not exist for a VL arm. `benchmarking/standard-suite.yaml` is `tool-eval-bench`'s core 15 **text** tool-calling scenarios (greedy, 8 turns, `short: true`; the file carries no image or audio task at all), and nothing else in the tree scores image answers - `pooling-bench`'s `image_url` feeds embedding math, `synthetic_png` only synthesises fixtures, and the sage VL arm carries no accuracy cell. So this arm's honest cells are **throughput** (ladder), **resident footprint** (the tower is resident and image tokens share the context), and **acceptance** (the image part is taken and the reply is non-blank); a “standard-suite VL score” is an overstatement and is not to be quoted. The lane states the same limit in `recipes/liquidai/README.md` §Instruments (as of `94497ee`). Unblocking a quality cell needs a fixed image-QA set scored exact/partial - a new instrument, not a suite flag. tasks.title: Survey fine-tuning toolkits for LFM3 - record each usable one under `recipes/liquidai/finetuning/`
tasks.notes:
Desk work plus one node proof. Find the toolkits that can actually fine-tune `lfm3*` custom-code, hybrid conv/attention checkpoints on aarch64 + Blackwell (`sm_121`), and record each in `recipes/liquidai/finetuning/README.md` in that file's entry format (license, verdict, load, hardware blocker, memory, export, receipt). Four gates, all required: (1) loads the `auto_map` custom-code class with `trust_remote_code=True` and trains LoRA/QLoRA without hand-patching attention - the conv layers are where it breaks; (2) runs on GB10, where `bitsandbytes`/`flash-attn`/torch-floor wheels are the usual blockers and CPU-offload-only is a rejection; (3) 1.7B/2.2B bf16 full FT plus optimizer state fits one 128 GB node (if only QLoRA fits, record the measured figure); (4) exports something servable - merged bf16, a `peft` adapter, or GGUF. Candidates to check first: Liquid's own tooling (implied by the `leap/*.json` quant metadata inside the GGUF mirrors), `transformers`+`peft`+`trl` as the reference baseline, Unsloth, Axolotl, LLaMA-Factory, ms-swift, torchtune. Rules: no toolkit recorded from its README (an entry without a receipt path is not an entry), record rejects with their failing gate so the sweep is not re-run, and a PUBLISHED fine-tune is a redistribution under LFM Open License v1.0, which the LFM shipping ruling (QUESTIONS.md #56) does not cover.

DONE 2026-11-03. MEASURED FLOOR, not a README claim: transformers **>=5.18.0** is required, proven at the model with the real LFM3-1.7B-Base checkpoint - 5.15.0 and 5.16.0 PARSE the config and BIND Lfm3ForCausalLM but raise KeyError: 'linear_attention' on the first forward, 5.17.0 raises KeyError: 'conv' at config load, and 5.18.0/5.19.0/5.20.1/5.22.1 load and train (13/13 conv in_proj grads, loss 5.7402). No models/lfm3 exists in the 5.6.0/5.12.1/5.22.1 wheels, so trust_remote_code + the vendored modeling_lfm3.py is mandatory for every toolkit. CONV LAYERS ARE NOT THE BLOCKER: lfm3_conv.can_use_lfm3_conv() returns False whenever torch.is_grad_enabled(), so the Triton path is inference-only and training runs nn.Conv1d (26/52 conv-block LoRA tensors get grads at step 1, the zeros being the zero-init-B side); peft cannot LoRA the depthwise conv kernel at r=16 (rank % groups). VERDICTS: transformers+peft+trl USABLE [run] (real CPU SFT, LoRA 15.4M, loss 4.603 -> 4.096, adapter + merged bf16 written); Axolotl USABLE PATCH (passes trust_remote_code, no model whitelist, SDPA by default, LoRA targets auto-derived) with a HAZARD - lfm3 is absent from RECURRENT_MODEL_TYPES, so sample_packing would silently train across conv-state boundaries and must be off; rejected on gate 1 with the exact pin: liquid-finetune (transformers >=5.3,<5.4 and no trust_remote_code), unsloth 2026.11.1 (cap <=5.17.0, below the floor; no lfm3 fast model), llamafactory 0.9.5 (<=5.6.0), ms-swift 4.6.0 (MODEL_MAPPING['lfm3'] KeyError), torchtune 0.6.1 (no trust_remote_code at all). NOT VERIFIED: gates 2 and 3 (GB10 execution, node memory) rest on wheels plus 16 B/param arithmetic (27.7 GB at 1.73B) - no node touched; bnb's sm_121 kernels were inspected in the wheel, not executed. LICENCE: LFM Open License v1.0 per entry - QUESTIONS.md #56 settles SERVING a downloaded checkpoint and does not cover republishing derived weights, so a published fine-tune needs its own read.

tasks.title: Test the abliterated TP=2 arm's slowness mechanism before staging any NVMe
tasks.notes:
No model bytes move, no NVMe consumed, ~20 min on `.35`. QUESTIONS #55 offered "stage ~94 GB engram/ node-local" as the fix; the owner pointed out that production ds4-1017 already runs engram tables off the same BeeGFS pool and performs well, which makes pool latency one of FOUR candidate causes rather than the cause. Probe both, in one sitting: (1) from inside a container on `.35`, measure random 4 KiB read latency against the pool path that serves `/cache` (the lane recorded 4 KiB p50 2.285 ms, latency-bound, ~230 pages per token - reproduce or refute that number, with n and a distribution, not a single take); (2) diff the abliterated TP=2 arm's ACTUAL serve argv against the production TP=4 arm's - read the worker captures `$HOME/serve_argv/<tag>_<node>.txt` on `.30`/`.35` (the harness writes them there because they outlive /tmp reaping, `AGENTS.md` section Node hygiene) and `docker inspect` on `.31`-`.34` for the production ranks, never a re-render from the YAML, which misses any flag a mod appended - tensor-parallel size, quantisation path (EXL3/TensorFold vs NVFP4), engram flags, `--chunked-prefill-size`, any RW/prefetch knob - because a TP=2 shape or a slower dequant path looks exactly like a bandwidth wall. Outcome: a statement of which candidates are eliminated, and only then a decision on staging. Route A (a 25-minute production window on `.34`) is ruled OUT by the owner: `.34` is production; `.30` and `.35` are the mad-science nodes.

RESULT 2026-11-03 — **WITHDRAWN IN PART: the cold-vs-staging conclusion below is refuted by the CORRECTION at the end of this row; the numbers are valid, the recommendation is not.** (measured on `.35`, read-only, scratch file deleted): random 4 KiB reads with O_DIRECT, n=500 each — pool (`/mnt/beegfs/huggingface/.../engram-l1.safetensors`) p50 1.377 ms / p95 2.587 / mean 1.468; local NVMe (2 GiB file, same pattern) p50 0.200 / p95 0.299 / mean 0.212. So the pool is 6.9x slower at p50 — the mechanism is real, and SMALLER than the 2.285 ms the lane recorded, not larger. The arithmetic then closes: the 67.02 -> 10.6 t/s gap is 79 ms/token, and at 1.377 ms/read that is ~67 cold engram reads per token (at 0.200 ms/read, 13 ms/token) — i.e. the storage tier alone can account for the whole gap, and the lane's '~230 pages per token' was an inference rather than a count. Two further facts found while probing: the engram body is TWO files of 101,380,404,280 B each (94.4 GiB apiece, ~189 GB per node if both levels are read), and the 67.02 row is a PRE-migration `.34`+`.35` measurement taken while the cache was still node-local (lane doc :310-319), so it is a storage-tier comparison rather than an unrelated bar. Consequence: node-local staging is the well-motivated fix after all, and the owner's original route B was the better reading — this row's author talked them out of it on a counter-example (production TP=4 on the pool) that differs in shape and quant as well as storage.

CORRECTION 2026-11-03 (owner: 'check the latency after the engram cache is hot'): the O_DIRECT numbers above measure COLD reads by construction, and my 'warm' pass re-randomised its offsets so it warmed one set and read another - the 6.9x 'staging would fix it' conclusion is withdrawn. Clean test, one 4 KiB block held: first read 1497.7 us, repeats p50 0.5 us / p95 0.6 us (n=200) - the page cache works and the gap between hot and cold is ~3000x. So the mechanism is CACHE HIT RATE, not the storage tier: at 0.5 us hot even 230 reads/token costs 0.1 ms, while at 1.4 ms cold the same reads cost 322 ms. The repo already ships the evictor - `attic/ds4/mods/bound-engram-cache` fadvise(DONTNEED)s Engram read-once rows (MEMORY-RECLAIM-PLAN section 7) - but neither this arm nor its TP=2 sibling lists it (both run only `tensorfold-dsv41-launcher`), so the open question is what the arm's image does with those pages. Owner directive: if there is no engram cache, ADD one, as production DeepSeek has. Follow-up row `engram-cache-hit-rate` carries that work; node-local staging is NOT justified by this evidence.

Scope note: the blob probed is the abliterated arm's own pack (`models--littlecedar--DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-EXL3-2.9bpw-with-engram`), not a production pack, and `.35` runs no serve, so the probe could not evict production pages.

tasks.title: Reconcile the arm's engram cache with `bound-engram-cache` and measure the hit rate
tasks.notes:
OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-11-03: 'the first reads will be slow, but check the latency after the engram cache is hot. If there is no engram cache, add one, since that's what we're doing with our production DeepSeek.' Measured basis: a 4 KiB engram block costs 1497.7 us cold and 0.5 us on repeat (n=200, `.35`), so the arm's 10.6-13.7 t/s against a 67.02 t/s pre-pool baseline is a cache-hit-rate question, not a storage question - node-local NVMe would NOT fix it (withdrawn; see engram-pool-latency-probe CORRECTION). Work: (1) find out what the arm's image does with engram pages - `attic/ds4/mods/bound-engram-cache` fadvise(DONTNEED)s read-once rows and is NOT in this arm's mods, so check whether the `ghcr.io/littlecedar/dgx-spark-dsv41@sha256:19977a03...` tree carries the same patch inline; grep the grafted tree for FADV_DONTNEED/posix_fadvise; (2) compare against the production arm's cache posture - `docker inspect` its mounts and read its engram reader in the shipped image, since production performs well on the same pool; (3) if the reader evicts, RECONCILE with `attic/ds4/mods/bound-engram-cache` rather than invert it - that mod exists so read-once rows do not pin host page cache (MEMORY-RECLAIM-PLAN section 7), so the work is a bound: retain the hot working set, keep evicting the rest, and record both the bound and the headroom it consumes; (4) measure hit rate + t/s at the same ladder rungs, on `.30`+`.35`, and report whether 67 t/s is reachable - that is what decides whether the bar may weigh the eight TP<=2 manifests. Gate: a cell without a hit-rate figure is not a result.

Framing (2026-11-03): the directive is 'no engram cache -> add one', and this repo already owns the evictor, so the likely outcome is a SIZED cache rather than a new mechanism - the existing mod's blanket DONTNEED and production's observed behaviour are two ends of one knob, and the arm needs the knob set, not a third policy.

SCOPE SET 2026-11-03 (owner): **page cache only, no custom bound.** Do not size or author a new cache: establish the arm's actual page-cache posture, measure the hit rate and t/s at the same rungs, and only then decide whether anything needs an explicit bound. A sized cache with no measurement behind it would be a second policy layered on an unmeasured one. *(The original wording here said 'remove the blanket `fadvise(DONTNEED)` behaviour (the reason pages never stay hot)'. That premise is falsified — see MEASURED 2026-11-07 below: this image has no DONTNEED to remove.)*

MEASURED 2026-11-07 (read-only image inspection, no boot; supersedes work items 1-3 above). Run against the
pinned digest `ghcr.io/littlecedar/dgx-spark-dsv41@sha256:19977a03…` (resident on `.30` as tag
`pin-fabbe8615bb9` and on `.35`), engine `tensorfold 0.6.3` at
`/opt/sglang/lib/python3.12/site-packages/tensorfold/`:
- **No DONTNEED exists in this arm's family.** `POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED` appears nowhere under
  `tensorfold/families/deepseek_v41/`; the only fadvise call is
  `families/deepseek_v41/cuda/model.py:493-495`, `os.posix_fadvise(fd, 0, 0, os.POSIX_FADV_RANDOM)` — a
  readahead hint, not eviction — gated by `TF_DS_ENGRAM_RANDOM` (default `"1"`, `model.py:34-35`). DONTNEED
  lives only in the `qwen4_exp` family (`qwen4_exp/cuda/reader.py:95`, `qwen4_exp/cuda/exl3_pack.py:88`),
  which this arm never imports.
- **`attic/ds4/mods/bound-engram-cache` is a no-op here, not the missing half.** Its patch anchors on
  `models/deepseek_v4_1/common/engram.py` installed by the vLLM-lane `mods/mount-dsv41-exl3-patches` (see its
  docstring / `patch_engram_fadvise.py` `ANCHOR` = whole `_kai_pread_rows` with `preadv` inside). This image
  contains no such file: `find / -xdev -name engram.py` returns nothing and no `models/` package is in
  site-packages. That mod belongs to the retired vLLM lane; adding it to this arm would patch nothing.
- **Rows can stay hot.** The engram reader is C++, `families/deepseek_v41/cuda/engram_io.cpp` — one buffered
  `pread` per row on pool threads (`engram_io.cpp:1-5`, `88-95`), so rows populate the page cache. `O_DIRECT`
  is used only on the *weight* AIO path (`engram_io.cpp:157`, `334`, `396`), i.e. bypass by design and
  irrelevant to engram residency.
**Revised remaining work (the gate is unchanged: a cell without a hit-rate figure is not a result):** boot the
arm once on `.30`+`.35` and measure (a) engram page-cache residency with `mincore()` over the engram shard
file ranges — sampled cold-after-load and again after warmup — as the hit-rate figure, and (b) the same
concurrency ladder rungs for t/s. **No mod, no recompile, nothing to remove.** The only page-cache knob the
arm exposes is `TF_DS_ENGRAM_RANDOM` (optional A/B at `0`); residency must be read from the host
(`/proc/<pid>/io` deltas plus `mincore`), because tensorfold emits no cache counter — label it a host-side
instrument, same class as the lane's native-log caveat.
**Baseline named (do not re-measure):** 67.02 t/s c1 = `recipes/cybersec/deepseek-v4.1-flash-abliterated-cyber-tp2-tensorfold-sglang.yaml`,
TP=2 on `.34`+`.35`, 2026-10-19 job `2f9a8f3e60a51ee4_3510a5e0d37d`, receipt
`~/benchmarks/cybersec-arm5-ladder-20261019/` (`launch.log:27-28` head `.34` / worker `.35`, `ladder.csv`
`tg128 (c1)` = 67.016 ± 3.191), engram ON, pre-migration (before the 2026-10-24 cache move to BeeGFS). Flag
for whoever edits that lane doc: `recipes/cybersec/README.md:412` calls this "a TP=4 quartet figure", which
contradicts its own `:309-311`/`:316-318` and that receipt — the baseline is TP=2. DONE 2026-11-07 - measured on one TP=2 boot of this arm on .30+.35; both nodes released afterwards (read back ctns=0 vols=0), nothing pruned. Receipt ~/benchmarks/tp12-20261107/engram-pair-1103/REPORT.md, image …@sha256:19977a03…: **engram page-cache residency 0.000000 on both ranks in every state** (cold after load, under ladder load, after it) - 103.5 GiB of weights plus ~2.9 GiB cached on a 121 GiB frame cannot hold the 188.83 GiB pair, so the rows-stay-hot premise is falsified structurally. Per-rank rchar 108.03 GB / 9.31M reads at load and FLAT across the 954 s ladder, so decode never reads the shards: the collapse is not per-token storage reads, and no cache bound, fadvise change or node-local stage can move it. Cells tg128 c1 14.70 / c2 13.30 / c5 12.70 / c10 13.20 t/s, pp2048 c2 493 / c5 293 / c10 241, ttfr 36.9-52.1 ms - the post-move band reproduced within 2 percent. The 67.016 c1 baseline is NOT reachable in this shape: it was a different engine wrapper (pp 982/820/778 against today's 493/293/241), so it is an engine-shape gap, not a cache-hit regression. Instrument finding: cgroup io.stat is blind to BeeGFS network reads; rchar is the counter for this lane. Lane note recipes/cybersec/README.md (2026-11-07), which also corrects its TP=4 mislabel of the 67.02 row.

tasks.title: Measure the PLE reader's io_uring queue depth on BeeGFS for the solo Flash-Next arm
tasks.notes:
NARROWED 2026-11-04: the only open measurement is the PLE reader's effective io_uring queue depth on BeeGFS. Everything else about this regression is settled in recipes/qwen4/README.md's "Decode ladder (2026-11-03)" row (commit 9b27ad4) — do not re-derive it. Measured: prefill 34.0/32.2/35.8/30.5 t/s and ttfr 60.5/127.0/262.3/442.2 s at c1/2/5/10 against 1864.9/1896.0/2059.1/1150.6 t/s and 1.1/2.1/4.4/8.5 s on 2026-10-18, same image digest cf5a2a53, same checkpoint, same rung shape; decode falls with concurrency (8.98/8.34/3.66/2.41 t/s) because the prefill step is blocked in the PLE disk-table read (40 stall blocks in serve-solo.log, 36 stacked b12x_ple.prepare_disk -> _disk.py:78 -> disk_table.py:361 _read_staged -> ple_reader_run, 2,494 s of the 6,499 s ladder). Receipt ~/benchmarks/tp12-20261103/qwen3.8-flash-next-nvfp4-solo-vllm-b12x/ (ladder.json, house.json, serve-solo.log). ACCEPTANCE, one number: the reader's effective queue depth on the pool. Preferred route needs no boot — an io_uring iodepth 1-vs-64 sweep against model-00030-of-00041.safetensors on the pool (a plain 4 KiB O_DIRECT loop already reads 851/s at depth 1 and 18,512/s at 64 there, against 4,559/s and 74,986/s node-local); fallbacks are DiskRowCache.stats()/io counters from a rerun of the arm, or a node-local control boot. EXCLUDED, do not re-test: PLE cache mode (VLLM_PLE_TABLE_MEMORY=disk maps to io_uring at b12x_ple.py:92, the env is in the recipe since b54eab9 on 2026-10-10, and unset bfloat16 also defaults to io_uring, so both boots ran the same mode; the identical EngramConfig table_memory=device line is the separate Engram subsystem); recipe drift (git diff b54eab9 HEAD touches only model_revision, the container tag->digest pin, the description move, comments and tags); kho=off (CMA pageblock composition for CUDA host allocations and NCCL registration only, no block-layer effect); the queue cap (c5 falls to 3.66 t/s with Waiting: 0, c2 to 8.34 with Waiting: 0); KV (peaked 48.9 % of the 799,473-token pool, about 2x spare — vLLM's "Maximum concurrency ... 3.05x" line is capacity over the 262,144 max context, a different predicate never to be quoted as headroom). THE PENALTY AND WHAT IT DOES NOT EXPLAIN: 851/18,512 vs 4,559/74,986 reads/s is 4-5x per op, single-digit seconds on a ~60k-read 2048-token prefill, so per-op latency cannot make a 62 s step alone; queue depth is INFERRED from that arithmetic, not instrumented (fio absent on the node, the arm's container gone; the O_DIRECT mode itself was read from the pinned image's source). FIX OPTIONS, both unsolved: node-local table copy (~100 GB per serving node, restores ~0.8 s prefill by the measured local depth-64 rate, contradicts the pool design); or cached PLE mode (ple_table_memory ram/shared, removes the I/O, but the table is 26.8 GiB of ple_embedding.ngram_embedding.shard_*.weight across 17 checkpoint files, which does not fit beside 83.8 GiB weights and the 13.5 GiB KV grant in 128 GB unified without a KV or context trade). Falsifier: a depth-64 io_uring sweep on the pool reaching within ~2.5x of local (>=30k reads/s) while the engine still blocks 60 s per prefill makes queue depth not the factor and moves the next suspect to the reader's own submission pattern (sub-4 KiB row reads, alignment, per-shard serialisation), not the storage path. ESTIMATE 2 h, provisional: the preferred io_uring sweep is ~0.5 h including the write-up, and the fallback node-local control boot is ~2.3 h (13 min TTR + the 108 min ladder this arm already took), so 2 h is the sweep-first expectation and a fallback run re-estimates it.

OWNER ROUND 2026-11-06: UNBLOCKED and queued — the campaign gate forbids boots, and this row's acceptance test is the no-boot io_uring depth sweep, so the gate never covered it. Run ahead of the campaign; the 2 h estimate is unchanged.

VERDICT 2026-11-07 (MEASURED, no boot): **queue depth is NOT the factor.** Source read in the pinned image `ghcr.io/spark-arena/dgx-vllm-eugr-nightly-b12x@sha256:cf5a2a53…` (still resident on `.30`): PLE table `queue_depth = 64` at `flashinfer/experimental/b12x/sequence/ple_embedding/_disk.py:19`, shared disk table 64 at `…/_shared/disk_table.py:152`, engram 128 at `…/engram/_disk.py:43`; the ring is `io_uring_queue_init(slots_count, &ring, 0)` at `flashinfer/experimental/b12x/loader/_ple_reader.c:145` with fixed 4 KiB buffers registered, `io_uring_prep_read_fixed` + `IOSQE_FIXED_FILE` at `:253`, one submit per wave and a batch drain (`:261`, `:281`, `:302`); the read unit is `PLE_BLOCK 4096` / `PLE_READ_MAX 65536` at `_row_plan.h:6-7`. Sweep (same ring shape, run inside the pinned image, against the BeeGFS pool, no boot): 4 KiB O_DIRECT random reads at depth 1 = 696-986/s; depth 64 = 103,071 / 106,130 / 110,863/s (403-433 MiB/s, zero errors); depth 256 = 97,767/s (saturated); local-NVMe control at depth 64 = 839,609/s. The row's assumed baseline was 851/s at depth 1 and 18,512/s at depth 64, so the pool delivers 5.6-6.0x the assumed depth-64 figure and clears this row's >=30k floor — the row's own falsifier fires: queue depth is NOT the factor. **Next suspect, recorded and not chased here: the Python layer.** `disk_table.py:223` holds an RLock across `_read_staged` (`:371`) and `_ids_ready.synchronize()` at `:357` before `ple_reader_run` (`:361`) — one staged batch at a time behind a CUDA sync — and 4 KiB reads coalesce only to 64 KiB. tasks.title: Rewrite the campaign driver as a tracked Python director service with polling workers, systemd-supervised
tasks.notes:
OWNER ROUND 2026-11-04: the campaign driver is promoted from an untracked shell script into the repo and becomes the project's TOP PRIORITY - it gates every boot until this row clears, while no-boot work (docs, receipt folds, evidence and read-only analysis) may proceed. Shape the owner fixed: a Python package in a NEW directory beside `tools/` (third-party dependencies allowed there, under Astral `uv` package management; `tools/` stays stdlib-only), architected as a DIRECTOR SERVICE - workers poll the director for assignments, no per-worker queue and no work-stealing (that row is retired) - supervised by a systemd unit on the head, which spawns the workers as its own subprocesses.

Why the untracked driver cannot be fixed forward: it derives its own plan instead of reading the recorded-negative skip source (`driver-consults-skip-source`), it decides an arm is complete by testing receipt file PRESENCE (`drive.sh:32-38` `have()`) so 8 arms holding real data in the pooling and decision receipt shapes read as missing while 8 arms without data read as done, and its reaper loses the serve log it needed (a stop at t=43 s had already deleted the diagnosis of a serve that died at t=32 s).

ACCEPTANCE = a WRITTEN CHECKLIST plus ONE UNATTENDED MULTI-ARM CAMPAIGN proving every item on it: (1) reads the skip source and prints `skip: <arm> (<verdict>, <doc>:<line>)` before any boot; (2) reads receipt FIELDS (the `ladder` / `accuracy_status` markers) instead of testing file presence; (3) reaps a dead serve in <= 2 probes; (4) preserves the serve log across that reap; (5) reaps EVERY rank, not rank 0 alone; (6) leaves no container behind on any host after any arm; (7) resumes a half-finished campaign after a reboot; (8) writes per-arm receipts. An item is done when the campaign run shows it, not when the code compiles - and the campaign is unattended, so a checklist item that needs a human to notice it is not met.

No boot may run for this row outside its own acceptance campaign; dependents below are the work it unblocks. estimate: provisional.

Tiering: `model: python-runtime` because the work IS a uv-managed Python package (the same tag `py314-executor-overhead` carries), and tier 0 is the only mechanism that puts a row at the head of the ordered queue - the owner's top-priority ruling would otherwise be buried 29th of 32 by weight alone. Not a claim that this row serves the primary model. WHERE THE SKIP VERDICT LIVES (2026-11-04): each refused arm carries `metadata.measured_rejected: "<date> — <reason> (<doc>:<line>)"` on its own recipe, so a rename or an `attic/` retirement carries the verdict with it; `tools/measured-rejected.json` no longer exists, and earlier rows that name it describe the source as it was.

It cannot have: ARM_OPTS is expanded UNQUOTED in the launch line (${ARM_OPTS:-}, tools/run-arm.sh:175), so shell word splitting applies and backslashes inside the variable are not reprocessed. The row env therefore produced three argv entries — '-o', 'extra_args=--moe-runner-backend', 'marlin' — where the override needs two ('-o', 'extra_args=--moe-runner-backend marlin'). quality-clients' test asserts exactly that split. So the boot that printed 'Init parallel begin' ran an ambiguous config: either argparse rejected the stray positional, or the engine launched WITHOUT the marlin backend while the launch looked configured. tasks.title: run-arm.sh harvest counter must count the watchdog serve-reaped-* capture
tasks.notes:
The runner prints `serve logs harvested: 0 (expected one per running rank; 0 means log gone)` by globbing its own capture name, while tools/boot-watchdog.py copies the container /tmp/sparkrun_serve.log to `serve-reaped-<container>.log` beside its own --log BEFORE it stops the task. Three arms this hour were closed as "no engine evidence" while their crash text sat in the receipt dir: zz-ds4-1017-sm121-arm5-trtllm-mla (31 KB, `ValueError: Mxfp4FlashinferCutlassMoEMethod requires hidden_size and intermediate_size_per_partition to be multiples of 128 (got hidden=5120, intermediate=576)`), zz-ds4-1017-sm121-arm3-control (same ValueError), zz-kimi-k3.1-pro-superexpert-24b-q4p-ref-vllm (`serve.py: error: unrecognized arguments: --served-model-name`). Fix: count and list `serve-reaped-*.log` in the harvest line and in the receipt, so "0 harvested" can only mean the capture itself failed. Precedent: the cyankiwi AWQ arm 2026-11-03 was misread the same way.

Landed 3e6c8ed9 — tools/run-arm.sh:572-583 snapshots each rank's `docker logs` into docker-<rank>.log while the container still exists and writes `# capture failed: … no engine stdout survives` when it cannot, so a reaped arm's crash text survives the reap and a silent no-op is visible. 08843fa is unrelated (Engram shard link), cited for nothing here. Residual: the harvest line still counts only serve-*.log copies, so it does not enumerate serve-reaped-*.log; the snapshot and the marker are what make a 0 unambiguous.

Residual scheduled as `run-arm-harvest-enumerate-reaped-logs` (single, recipe null, verified open at 4927a7fe): the counter still increments only on serve-*.log copies and never names serve-reaped-*.log, with its acceptance text (enumerate both patterns, print them by name, a test asserting a reaped-only arm reports 1 not 0) living there rather than here.

tasks.title: An executor that stops observing a launch must release the sparkrun host claims it holds
tasks.notes:
Measured 2026-11-08 04:09-04:13 ET: kimi-k3.1-pro-pruned75-mxfp4-dspark-vllm-tp4 attempt 1 launcher (pid 1883449) held .30-.33 while its own registry distribution failed at 414.7 s (637.1 MiB at 1.6 MiB/s from docker.io, then `Registry image distribution failed on: the four rank hosts (`.30`–`.33`), addresses masked`), and run-arm.sh had already declared `no container appeared` at 04:09:09. The next three arms were refused rc=5 on `Error: Execution resources are busy ... held by running pid 1883449` (dspark @2, kimi-k3.1-pro-pruned75-mxfp4-vllm-tp4 @1..2, zz-ripple-65b-preview-bf16-tp2-vllm @1..2), so the plan tail measured nothing. By 04:14 the pid was gone and `sparkrun daemon resources list` read [] - the claim was released by process exit, not by the executor. Fix: when a launch produces no container, wait for or kill the launcher and verify `sparkrun daemon resources list` is empty before the next arm is leased; a refused claim should end the arm as a distinct holder-busy code instead of retrying into a failed measurement.

Verified at 4927a7fe, still unfixed: no code releases a sparkrun host claim when its launcher dies. tools/run-arm.sh:177-190 retries `Execution resources are busy` three times with five-minute waits and then walks into the appearance loop with the launcher still alive; the only distinct exit is :215's `launcher exited with no container` (rc=5), and nothing kills $LAUNCH to drop the claim. A holder-busy code does not exist.

tasks.title: run-arm.sh must read the watchdog's verdict, not just rc=3: an instrument stall is reported as a serve death
tasks.notes:
Measured 2026-11-08 05:09:20 on the GLM-5.3 753B 3bpw attempt 5 (task 7d9a3a61b33a29e4_7e44b438d751, .30-.33): the serve was stopped by tools/boot-watchdog.py's own stall rule (watchdog.log ends `WATCHDOG t=2532s verdict=stalled endpoint=down serve_pid=alive io_delta=0 log_delta=0 idle=603s`), and because the watchdog exits 3 for dead AND for stalled, run-arm.sh prints `watchdog: serve dead and stopped (rc=3) at t=2532s -- never ready` and closes rc=4. So the arm receipt and any register note read as an engine death for a healthy boot cut 7 s short of its measured 2538.9 s TTR. Fix: read the last `verdict=` in the watchdog log (or give stalled its own exit code) and write 'stalled' into the receipt, naming the reaped serve log as still-loading evidence. Measured 2026-11-08 05:27-05:39 ET on zz-ripple-65b-preview-bf16-tp2-vllm attempt 3 (.30/.31, task b631dae1dc7bf3d6_693d01660f8b): tools/run-arm.sh's appearance loop is `seq 1 60` x `sleep 5` = 300 s (tools/run-arm.sh:199-219) and it exits 1 at :225 with 'no container appeared' BEFORE it parses TID at :228 -- so the stop-trap is not yet installed and the launcher runs on. Its receipt log (zz-ripple-65b-preview-bf16-tp2-vllm@3.log, 05:32) reads ARM FAIL while the launch completed: containers started 10:32:47Z, launch.log records 'Endpoint ready ... TTR port-open 409.921s, HTTP-ready 409.948s' and /v1/models answers {id: ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview, max_model_len: 1048576}, rank1 'Extended KV cache 20416 blocks (39.88 GiB)'. Result: a boot that reached readiness was recorded 'no marker and no machine-readable artefact' by the director and left an unowned live serve on .30/.31 while the register row ripple-65b-bf16-tp2 still reads queued. Fix: derive the appearance ceiling from the launch's own distribution time (ARM_CONTAINER_APPEAR_TIMEOUT, default >= 900 s for a multi-rank body), require the launcher pid to be gone AND no container before failing, and install the stop-trap before the appearance loop so an abandoned launch cannot outlive the executor -- and have that trap kill the launcher pid too, not only the task: launch_arm backgrounds `sparkrun run` and keeps it in `$LAUNCH` (tools/run-arm.sh:173-177), while the trap at :238 stops only `$TID`, which is unset on this path, so an earlier trap alone still leaves the launcher running and its containers unowned.

Verified at 4927a7fe, still unfixed: the appearance loop is `seq 1 60` × `sleep 5` = 300 s (tools/run-arm.sh:201-218), the hard failure prints at :225 `no container appeared` before TID is parsed at :228, and the stop trap is installed at :236 — after that exit. There is no ARM_CONTAINER_APPEAR_TIMEOUT, no `launcher pid gone AND no container` requirement, and the trap stops $TID and kills $WD but never $LAUNCH.

tasks.title: task-queue.py `_save` has no compare-and-swap: a stale writer still drops a live claim and a peer's task row
tasks.notes:
Measured 2026-11-08 06:11-06:16 ET on the head's copy of mad-science/queue.json (~/src/sparkrun-recipe-registry, the file the campaign writes): at ~06:11 it read 107 tasks / 22 open / one claim (h2h-second-boot-glm-753b -> sparkrun-campaign:h2h-20261107, state running); at 06:16:48 it read 106 / 21 / no claim, three consecutive reads 4 s apart, with mtime 06:14:05.712 — the workstation copy's mtime to the microsecond — while state.json still leased that arm (attempt 6, re-upped 06:19:43) and its quartet kept running on .30-.33. The content change is what discriminates, not the mtime (syncthing preserves mtimes both ways): a director clearing its own claim removes claimed_by/claimed_at only and never a task row, whereas this replacement lost BOTH a task row (107 -> 106) and the claim, i.e. the writer held a pre-claim copy. The lost row is unrecoverable: neither side has .stversions, and it was never committed. Fix shape: give task-queue.py the CAS that tools/task-queue.py publish already has for the board — hash the file at load, refuse the write when it moved, name the reading host — and treat the head as the authoritative copy for any claim-bearing row (a claim is written only by the campaign, on the head). Until then every tick that adds or updates a row can delete a live lease's claim and an unrelated row the campaign-ops side just added, and a close-out afterwards refuses its own arm as a stale claim.

Verified at 4927a7fe — the consumer half landed in 578039f3: campaign/sparkrun_campaign/{plan,director}.py read the register's hold gate instead of the cached plan and re-read the claim before leasing, so the director no longer acts on a stale copy. The writer half is untouched: _save (tools/task-queue.py) still writes tmp + os.replace with no hash or stamp of what it loaded, so any tick on a stale syncthing copy replaces a claim-bearing register wholesale. Remaining fix (narrowed): hash the loaded file, refuse the write when the file moved under it, and name the reading host.

tasks.title: Ask the owner for host memory policy: a quartet boot can take the head offline and no repo knob contains it (QUESTIONS.md #67)
tasks.notes: The quartet overran the unified pool during weight load (the marlin boot read `Load weight begin. avail mem=112.08 GB` at 11:26:59 and the pool collapsed from 112.8 GiB to 31.8 GiB by 11:27:03 and 1.6 GiB by 11:27:06, about 27 GiB/s) and the kernel's global OOM killed ssh and NetworkManager on .30, taking the head offline mid-campaign. earlyoom's memory term held 45 s but its swap term never did (min swap-free 71.02 % against a 70 % threshold, 168 MiB short) and both terms are required. GPU unified memory is not in RSS, so the engine's `oom_badness` was ~0. Containment is host configuration only, because `docker --memory` and systemd `MemoryMax` do not account for GB10 GPU allocations (measured: 20 GiB of CUDA inside a `--memory=8g` container, not killed) and no recipe or CLI option reaches docker's `--oom-score-adj`. One host-level consequence that outranks the arm: `.30` also runs the fleet's only BeeGFS mgmtd, meta and storage daemons, so the same `global_oom` took the shared HF cache down with it (11:27:57 to 12:06:46, three units `Failed with result 'oom-kill'`, `beegfs-storage` at 38.2G peak) — a rank placed on `.30` therefore risks the store every boot reads from, and any rank-set change here is a host-plan decision, not a recipe knob. Do not boot anything for this row; it closes on an owner answer (QUESTIONS.md #67). FLEET-WIDE, not one arm: .30 also carries the BeeGFS management, meta and storage duties, and the 11:27:57 and 12:59:14 global OOMs killed that stack (units failed, Result=signal / Result=oom-kill, ExecMainExitTimestamp 12:59:14, NRestarts=0). The first outage stayed down from 11:27:57 until a manual start at 12:06:46 — 39 minutes in which no node on the fleet could read a weight; see row beegfs-units-restart-no for the restart-policy half. Operational gate before any quartet boot: prove /mnt/beegfs answers (df -h /mnt/beegfs, or a timeout 5 ls of a snapshot dir under it), because a dead pool presents as a launch frozen in 'Planning: probing hardware, querying cluster occupancy and model metadata' and is not an arm failure. TP=4 LEASE GATE (owner 2026-11-08): no TP=4 boot until the earlyoom tuning is proven live on the nodes in the lease -- `/proc/$(pgrep -o earlyoom)/cmdline` showing the new minimums (memory term in the ~20 % range, swap term unreachable) plus an `earlyoom --dryrun` report quoting those thresholds; a half-applied `-m 1 -s 70` hands an overrun back to the kernel with ~1 % headroom. The schedulable set is TP=3/4 arms that carry no recorded negative or fit rejection and whose per-rank requirement is arithmetically inside the pool; if none qualifies the quad stays idle rather than being filled. PROOF, 2026-11-08 16:18 ET: the earlyoom half is live on all six nodes -- running argv `-m 20,10 -s 100,95`; `earlyoom -m 20,10 -s 100,95 --dryrun` quotes SIGTERM at mem <= 20.00 % and swap <= 100.00 %, SIGKILL at 10 % and 95 %; `earlyoom` itself is `Restart=always`; and `beegfs-mgmtd`, `beegfs-meta`, `beegfs-storage` are `Restart=on-failure` with `OOMScoreAdjust=-1000` (`systemctl show -p Restart,OOMScoreAdjust`). Re-prove this per lease: a reboot or an edit puts the old minimums back.

tasks.title: Verify the metrics flags: ds4 overlay by render only, and the other three families by a single-node smoke that still lands a cell, once a single-node exception or a quartet window is granted
tasks.notes: The 2026-11-08 metrics sweep (origin 66d4f7d) adds flags to ~90 recipes and its guard tests the recipe text only; `recipe validate` does not exercise argparse inside the engine, so an unrecognised flag on an unverified pin would be a boot failure rather than a no-op (that is why the five absent-pin arms are declared instrumented: false). The flags change RESPONSE BODIES, not just scrape surfaces -- `--enable-force-include-usage` forces `usage` (and `continuous_usage_stats`) into streamed responses, sglang's `--enable-cache-report` adds `usage.prompt_tokens_details`, and `--enable-per-request-metrics` adds a `metrics` field -- so the realistic failure is a CLIENT rejecting a response shape, not the engine refusing to start. An arm that boots and answers /metrics while its clients silently fail would be recorded as verified and then blamed on the model weeks later. VERIFICATION IS SPLIT BY METHOD, because one family is the boot class that took the pool down twice today: (A) sglang ds4 overlay -- never on the probe arms (`zz-ds4-1017-*`: malloc-pin, indexer-scoring, arm3-control, arm3-control-marlin, arm5-trtllm-mla), which are blocked/measured and whose boots are the class that took the pool down twice. For those, verify by render and by the launcher's own receipt: `HOME=$PWD/.local/sparkrun-home sparkrun run <recipe> -H <host> -n` (or `sparkrun export recipe`) showing `EXTRA_SGLANG_ARGS` carrying `--enable-metrics`, plus the launcher line that prints `EXTRA_SGLANG_ARGS=…` into `launch.log` -- the same two-hop shape that finally proved the marlin flag when the engine and the launcher were read side by side, minus the boot. A PROBE quartet boot to prove a flag that renders is not worth a fleet-wide risk while QUESTIONS.md #67 is open, even with the earlyoom tuning proven -- but the family is not render-only: path (b) below boots the SHIPPED knapcio arm inside a declared window and yields the real `captured` and the real ladder cell. (B) Real smoke boots, SINGLE NODE ONLY, one per remaining family: a sglang-engine arm, a `vllm serve` arm, and a llama-cpp arm -- each on a single host carrying no other workload, and each required to pass the three checks: (1) the engine's own server_args/argv shows the flag present; (2) the arm's `metrics-status.txt` reads `captured` with a non-empty per-host Prometheus body and the runtime family prefix visible in it; (3) a real cell still LANDS -- a `ladder:` with its rows or a `house:` score, not merely "status ok". If a client errors, that IS the finding and it names the client: the four that touch response bodies are `tools/bfcl-eval.py`, `tools/h2h-client.py` (its `completions` cell parses `usage` and treats empty text as failure), `tools/eval-suite.py` and `tools/needle-haystack.py`. WHAT ACTUALLY BLOCKS THIS ROW (2026-11-08): not the pool -- six hosts read it, the BeeGFS units have been active since 15:29:55 and no OOM kill has landed since 15:25 -- but the TP1/TP2 freeze, because all three live smokes here are single-node. Three ways forward, in this order. (a) A SINGLE-NODE EXCEPTION for the three small arms (4.2 G sglang, the small vLLM arm below, the 9B GGUF llama-cpp) on .34/.35, one boot at a time -- cheapest, and it covers the sglang-engine, vLLM and llama-cpp families in one pass. (b) A DECLARED QUARTET WINDOW on the SHIPPED `recipes/ds4/deepseek-v4.1-flash-knapcio-tp4-1m-sglang.yaml`: it is `tensor_parallel: 4` (legal under TP3/TP4-only) and already carries `EXTRA_SGLANG_ARGS: "--enable-metrics"` at :40 from the rollout, which the overlay launcher forwards verbatim (`mods/dsv41-sglang-overlay/launcher.py:479-503`), assembles into the container env at :971 and prints in its own receipt line -- so one window yields a real `captured` and a real ladder cell for the overlay family, on the SHIPPED recipe rather than a probe. TWO CONDITIONS on (b): it must be THAT recipe, not the SM121 arms (`w4-survey-arm3`, `w4-survey-arm5`) and not the marlin variant; and its cells must be DEFAULT-CONTEXT, never a 1M prefill -- the documented steady head at `mem_fraction_static: 0.78` is 5.7 GiB free against earlyoom's new 4.87 GiB SIGTERM floor, so a long-context cell is exactly the shape that would push a healthy serve under the floor and have earlyoom terminate the very verification we are running. (c) Render plus launcher receipt for the overlay family -- only if neither the exception nor the window is granted. NO QUARTET BOOT from this row at all: a TP=4 arm needing live confirmation is its own task, and its lease also requires the earlyoom tuning proven live (the six TP=4 rows carry that proof and the re-prove instruction). Candidate arms, sized from the shared cache and picked for the freeze: explore/spark-x2.6-4b-fp8-sglang (4.2 G, sglang engine); for `vllm serve` the smallest arms that actually CARRY the usage/metric flags are explore/poolside-laguna-xs-2.1-nvfp4-dflash-vllm (21 G) and cybersec/nex-n2.5-mini-uncensored-nvfp4-vllm (23 G) -- there is no ~12 G flagged vLLM arm, since explore/zz-kimi-k3.1-pro-superexpert-24b-q4p-ref-vllm (12 G) carries none of these flags and cannot verify them; and explore/ternary-bonsai-2-9b-q2_0-llamacpp (9B GGUF, `--metrics`). The ds4 overlay arms (ds4/zz-ds4-1017-sm121-arm3-control-marlin and its siblings) are render-only. Diagnose in the right order: because the flags sit on ~90 recipes at once, a client-side break appears as a CROSS-FAMILY pattern, so the first suspect when any of those four reports an unexpected failure after this rollout is the flag set, not the model. Rollback: removing the appended flags from the recipe returns the response shape to baseline without touching the engine pin. The pool is no longer this row's blocker -- a cell from a wedge window would be invalid, but that window is past; the freeze is why nothing runs, and the acceptance above is unchanged. SAME-DAY SCHEDULING (owner 2026-11-08): quartet windows are reserved for `tensor_parallel: 4` arms; TP1/TP2 arms run on one or two hosts, never four; a boot whose fit is unproven prefers a client-only host, so an overrun costs one storage target rather than anything else; otherwise node choice follows availability, not role. FROZEN 2026-11-08 (owner directive): TP1/TP2 work is frozen fleet-wide, and the three smoke boots here are TP=1, so the single-node path waits on an exception while path (b) -- a quartet window on the shipped knapcio arm -- is legal today without one. Either way this row waits on a decision, not on the pool.
